Sea-anemone nematocyst ICK toxin active on pain receptors (U-isophellitoxin-Tst2); neurotoxin family is right.
Box-jellyfish nematocyst ACE-inhibitory peptide; a nematocyst venom component and the bradykinin-potentiating peptide family is exactly right.

Hornet venom-gland crabrolin: Toxin-keyworded MCD-family mast-cell degranulating peptide, hemolytic on rat and guinea-pig erythrocytes; model called nontox -> false negative.
Carp endogenous isotocin hormone; the vasopressin/oxytocin family is venom-recruited (conopressins) but this is the physiological hormone -> false-positive.
Ant venom-gland myrmexin subunit; family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Rhinoceros-adder venom-gland PLA2 (group II); genuine venom family member.
Beetle endogenous antifungal chitin-binding peptide scarabaecin -> false-positive toxin call.
Uncharacterized blood-fluke secreted knottin with no toxin evidence; the ICK fold drove the neurotoxin call -> false-positive.
Cone-snail venom-duct elevenin (prey-neuropeptide mimic; elevenin family unmodeled so label is 'other'); conotoxin call is venom-correct but the family is approximate.

Tityus serrulatus venom-gland peptide 1; in vivo it diminishes locomotion and induces anxiety in mice, so tox on venom-gland origin plus animal-directed effect. UniProt places it in the NDBP superfamily (short AMP group 4), a modelled class, so Bradykinin-related peptide is the wrong bin.
Russell's viper venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor 4; venom Kunitz-type is exactly right. The nontox ground truth is the usual keyword gap on venom protease inhibitors.
King-cobra venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor (TCI); genuine venom Kunitz family member.

THIS IS THE ONE ROW IN THE BATCH RESTING ON THAT EXTENSION rather than on hemolysis proper; revert it to nontox if the rule is meant to stay strictly hemolytic. Turgencin has no UniProt family, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Malayan krait venom-gland PLA2 (group I); genuine venom family member.
Silkworm hemolymph protease inhibitor (immune, prophenoloxidase regulation), not venom; protease-inhibitor signal drove a venom-Kunitz call -> false-positive toxin.

Pig endogenous hormone TRH (pGlu-His-Pro-NH2, 3 residues); the natriuretic/BPP call on a tripeptide is spurious -> false-positive.

Tobacco-budworm virescein, a moricin-family hemolymph AMP of insect innate immunity, not a venom peptide. Brown snake's OWN plasma/liver coagulation factor X (endogenous S1 protease), not the venom prothrombin activator; Peptidase-S1 call shares a venom-recruited fold -> false-positive toxin.

Fly endogenous serpin 42Dd (Toll-pathway immune regulation, ovary) -> false-positive toxin call.
Hornet venom-gland phospholipase A1 (potently hemolytic, lethal); venom PLA1 family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Honeybee venom-gland secapin; family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call. A genuine venom component even though this entry is annotated 'nontoxic peptide'; cf. CE190, where the model called the sister secapin nontox.

Ant venom-gland U1-poneritoxin-Ni3d (ponericin-G family); the family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Flannel-moth venom-apparatus U-megalopygitoxin(2)-Mo9, Toxin-keyworded; binary call right, but the caterpillar 2 family is unmodeled ('other' was the label) and Scoloptoxin is a centipede family.
Russell's viper venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor; genuine venom Kunitz family member.
Hornet venom-gland phospholipase A1 VesT1.02 (hemolytic); venom PLA1 family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Scorpion venom-gland RK1, a Toxin-keyworded disintegrin-like peptide that blocks tumour-cell proliferation, migration and angiogenesis via integrins; model called nontox -> false negative.
Brown-snake venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor (textilinin-5); genuine venom Kunitz family member.

Bombina skin Maximins 4/H3 type 4: maximin-H3 shows strong hemolytic activity and the entry is Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, so tox under the hemolysis rule, even though maximin-4 itself is the mild member of the pair. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Stephens's banded snake venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor (stephenin-2); genuine venom Kunitz family member.

Ant venom-gland M-poneratoxin-Dq3a; UniProt bins it in the NDBP superfamily (ponericin-W subfamily), a modelled class, so Formicidae venom family is the wrong axis even though it is genuinely an ant venom peptide. Defensible confusion, not a biological error.
Cobra venom three-finger toxin (cytotoxin); genuine venom family member.
Scorpion venom-gland peptide Ctri10261; NDBP superfamily is exactly right.
Keelback venom-gland cysteine-rich venom protein (tigrin); CRISP family is exactly right.
Sea-anemone nematocyst Nav toxin (sea anemone short toxin type III, unmodeled so label is 'other'); the conotoxin call is a different venom family. Venom-correct, family wrong.

Feather-duster-worm SmCI, a tentacle-crown carboxypeptidase and serine protease inhibitor built from BPTI-Kunitz repeats. No venom apparatus and no animal-directed activity. Venom Kunitz call -> false positive.

Saddleback-caterpillar venom-spine toxin that is a venom-recruited FMRFamide-related peptide; the label follows the FARP fold family while the model followed the limacoditoxin venom naming. Venom-correct, family label genuinely ambiguous.

Human Speedy protein E3, an intracellular testis- and spleen-expressed Speedy/RINGO cell-cycle regulator with no secretion, no annotation and no toxin link. Wolf-spider venom-gland bradykinin-potentiating peptide (ACE inhibitor); BPP family is exactly right.

Mosquito salivary aegyptin-like anti-platelet protein: a blood-feeder feeding secretion that blocks host collagen-platelet binding; model called nontox -> false negative. Same blind spot as the July alboserpin and tick TAP rows.
Cone-snail conotoxin (A superfamily); genuine venom family member.
Common-tick salivary serpin Iripin-4 (blood-feeding secretion); serpin family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Medicinal-leech salivary hirudin-2 (thrombin inhibitor, blood-feeding anti-hemostatic); hirudin family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Fly male accessory-gland protease inhibitor (reproductive, paragonial peptide D), not venom -> false-positive.
Red-headed-krait venom-gland acidic phospholipase A2 2; Phospholipase family is exactly right. Keyword gap on the label side, same as CE156.
Freshwater-pearl-mussel BPTI/Kunitz protein 5, a shell-matrix protein of the nacreous layer expressed in the mantle. Biomineralisation, not venom. Venom Kunitz call -> false positive.
Jack-jumper ant venom-gland pilosulin-5 (histamine-releasing); Formicidae venom family is exactly right.
Wolf-spider venom lycosin-I; UniProt places it in the cationic peptide 04 (cupiennin) family, so the cationic-peptide call is exactly right.

Ant venom-gland M-poneritoxin-Nc3b, a Toxin-keyworded insecticidal ponericin (reversible paralysis in L.cuprina, PD50 26.4 nmol/g); model called nontox -> false negative. Note the model got the sister ponericin CE053 right.
Scorpion venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor LmKTT-1a (delta-KTx 2.1); genuine venom Kunitz family member.
Spider venom cationic peptide (met-lysine); broad 'cationic peptide' call is venom-correct, family approximate.

Goat lactotransferrin, an endogenous iron-binding exocrine and immune protein. Model called 'other', a tox call, so this is the July duck-transferrin failure repeating on a second transferrin: the family is a genuine hard-negative pool.
Hornet venom-gland mastoparan-VT7; MCD/mastoparan family is exactly right.
Sweat-bee venom-gland lasioglossin-3; the MCD/mastoparan call is the adjacent hymenopteran linear venom-peptide family. Venom-correct, family approximate.

Solitary-bee venom-gland macropin (the July lasioglossin precedent); UniProt bins it in the lasioglossin-like family, which is unmodeled, so 'other' was the right call and Cationic peptide is a specific wrong bin. Chemically defensible: macropin is a linear amphipathic melittin-like peptide.
Ant venom-gland ponericin Pa I1 (ponericin-G family); family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.

Scorpion 4 kDa defensin: dual-function, and it blocks potassium channels as well as being antimicrobial. Channel blockade is an animal-directed toxin activity (scorpion defensins are the CSaB ancestor of the alpha-KTx toxins), so toxic on the evidence even though it is hemolymph-derived with no venom-gland annotation. The invertebrate defensin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Cup-moth venom-spine limacoditoxin (vulnericin); model called nontox -> false negative.
Eel natriuretic peptide hormone — endogenous, not venom; right family but false-positive toxin call.
Scorpion venom-gland toxin-like protein 14; venom-gland origin makes the tox call right, but UniProt assigns no family and Scoloptoxin is a centipede family.

Hornet venom-gland phospholipase A1 (Vesp v 1), a major vespid venom allergen with hemolytic activity. UniProt places it in the AB hydrolase/lipase family, which is unmodeled (the Phospholipase class only absorbs PLA2-type names), so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Saw-scaled-viper venom-gland dimeric disintegrin schistatin-like subunit B, Toxin-keyworded platelet-aggregation inhibitor; same Disintegrin versus M12B parent-fold confusion as CE166.
Scorpion venom-gland non-disulfide-bridged peptide 5.6, Toxin-keyworded, cytolytic and weakly hemolytic; model called nontox -> false negative, and on a family it does model.
Mosquito salivary antigen-5 / venom allergen-1 (blood-feeding secretion, host immunomodulator); CRISP family is exactly right.
Cone-snail venom-duct conotoxin (T superfamily); model called nontox -> false negative.
Sea-anemone nematocyst Kunitz-type toxin (HMRG1); genuine venom Kunitz family member.

Manduca sexta moricin, an insect innate-immunity AMP (the explicit July nontox precedent), with no hemolysis or cytotoxicity reported, so the hemolysis rule does not reach it. NDBP call -> false positive: AMP chemistry read as venom-peptide chemistry.
Locust endogenous diuretic hormone locupressin (vasopressin/oxytocin family); right family, not venom -> false-positive.
Crown-of-thorns starfish venom-gland plancitoxin-1 (hepatotoxic DNase II); model called nontox -> false negative.
Scorpion venom-gland neurotoxin BmK A3-6; no effect on the channels tested, but venom-gland origin governs. UniProt assigns no family and short scorpion toxin superfamily is the taxon-standard bin.
Ant venom-gland ponericin-G4; family unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
White-lipped snake venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor; genuine venom Kunitz family member.
Wasp venom-gland Polybia-CP, chemotactic and cytotoxic to HEK293 cells; MCD family (protonectin subfamily) is exactly right.

Bombina skin Maximins 3/H16: Hemolysis and Cytolysis keyworded, and it encodes maximin-3, which is tumour-cytotoxic, anti-HIV and highly spermicidal. Both sibling precursors carrying the same maximin-3 (P83082, Q8JHE1) ARE Toxin-keyworded, so this nontox label is curator inconsistency. Bombinin family is unmodeled, so 'other' is the correct tox call.
Flannel-moth venom-apparatus megalopygitoxin; model called nontox -> false negative.
Cape-cobra venom-gland Kunitz-type inhibitor 2; venom Kunitz-type is exactly right. Keyword gap on the label side.
Mosquito salivary D7-related 3 (sequesters host response mediators, vasodilator); PBP/GOBP family is exactly right.
Bulldog-ant venom-gland myrmeciitoxin; Formicidae venom family is exactly right.
Forest-cobra venom-gland PLA2 (group I); genuine venom family member.
Silkworm endogenous chymotrypsin inhibitor (prophenoloxidase regulation, immune), not venom -> false-positive. Same pattern as the seed row CE198.
Mulga-snake venom-gland PLA2 (group I); genuine venom family member.
Mamushi venom-gland PLA2 (group II); genuine venom family member.
Scorpion venom-gland pantinin-1; NDBP superfamily is exactly right.
Funnel-web spider venom-gland hexatoxin magi-12 (neurotoxin 03 / Tx2 family, knottin); neurotoxin family is right.
